p2_b6.ocr: (adjusted by age) with a lower likelihood of reporting LTPA in both gen- ders, which is in agreement with previous studies con- ducted in Australia [16] and USA [29]. Gallant and Dorn [42] reported that marital status showed an influ- ential element in men’s health behavior. Our results are also consistent with Kaplan et al [29] who found that married subjects were less likely to be active than single, widowed, or divorced. The current study also found that education level (pri- mary or over) was related with LTPA and fitness activ- ity, which agrees with previous studies [14,17,32]. The Shanghai Women’s Health Study reported that women aged 40-70 years of age with more education were more likely to practice sports, but widows/divorced/separated were more likely to walk [17]. In contrast, Wong et al reported that people with lower educational level spent more time on walking than those with higher level [32].
